title: Full Bodycam Released in Footballer’s Fatal Car Crash
description:
Please follow us on X (Twitter): https://x.com/policeinsidertv

We add the AI content label at the beginning of the video because our voiceovers are generated with AI. The case and the bodycam footage itself is 100% real, and authentic, not AI generated.

That is an automated 911 call being sent by a football player’s iPhone after he was ejected from a Ford Expedition when it struck two power poles.
#news
--------------
About Us / Disclaimer: 

Police Insider provides unbiased and authentic footage of incidents captured on body cams. We believe this footage can be used as an educational guide for viewers. 

We only provide unique and original content that hasn’t been covered before on YouTube.

The raw footage for the videos on this channel have been obtained directly from the respective Police Departments. We as a media company have the right to use it commercially. Most incidents may require a fee associated with the request and take several days to process.

The channel is not affiliated with any law enforcement agency.

Our channel is compliant with YouTube's Fair Use Policy as we create a storyline and cut down several hours of long footage to a few minutes to bring out the most entertaining and educational parts, just like other channels such as Code Blue Cam, Real World Police, Active Police Cam, Blue Watch and Bodycam FIles.

The featured content is NOT intended to publicly shame, ridicule, or degrade the individuals involved or to glorify violence in any way.

Using all the witness statements in the surveillance camera videos, it was now easy for the investigator to map out exactly how the events unfolded. Right before 2.30 a.m., Chandler, along with her team members, consumed alcohol at Toppers. They left the bar and decided to go to the Waffle House near the gas station, beginning to race toward it, along with Jalen and his passenger, Tania. They eventually decided to skip it and then made a right turn onto Barnett Scholes Road, heading toward the next Waffle House. This was when Jalen followed Chandler closely in his Jeep and saw her hit two power poles before crashing down the roadway. The power lines then struck Jalen's car, and he stopped a little farther down the road. He then called Jamin, who arrived at the scene with other football players. And shortly after, Malcolm also drove through the fallen power lines, losing his front bumper in the middle of the road. Former University of Georgia star football player Jalen Carter is out of jail. Last night, he turned himself into Athens-Clark County jails. He faces charges in connection with a crash that killed his former. teammate and a university staff member. After the investigation, Jalen was charged with street racing and reckless driving. He later turned himself in, posted a $4,000 bond, and was released. He then entered a no contest plea agreement and was sentenced to 12 months of probation, a $1,000 fine 80-plus hours of community service and a defensive driving course. He was later drafted 9th overall by the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2003 NFL draft. On the other hand, Victoria filed a $5 million lawsuit against Jalen and the estate of Chandler, blaming them for racing even though both had histories of traffic offenses. Her lawsuit cited medical expenses of more than $170,000 and a total of $27,000 in lost wages. The claim has yet to be settled. She also sued the UGA Athletic Association for entrusting a rented SUV to Chandler, despite knowing her history of traffic violations. A settlement was later reached for $1.5 million. Devon's father also sued the UGA Athletic Association for $40 million for the same reasons, and that case remains active to date. YouTube thinks you'll love the video on screen. Click to watch now.

Using all the witness statements in the surveillance camera videos,
it was now easy for the investigator to map out exactly how the events unfolded.
Right before 2.30 a.m., Chandler, along with her team members, consumed alcohol at Toppers.
They left the bar and decided to go to the Waffle House near the gas station, beginning to race toward it,
along with Jalen and his passenger, Tania.
They eventually decided to skip it and then made a right turn onto Barnett Scholes Road,
heading toward the next Waffle House.
This was when Jalen followed Chandler closely in his Jeep and saw her hit two power poles before crashing down the roadway.
The power lines then struck Jalen's car, and he stopped a little farther down the road.
He then called Jamin, who arrived at the scene with other football players.
And shortly after, Malcolm also drove through the fallen power lines, losing his front bumper in the middle of the road.
Former University of Georgia star football player Jalen Carter is out of jail.
Last night, he turned himself into Athens-Clark County jails.
He faces charges in connection with a crash that killed his former.
teammate and a university staff member. After the investigation, Jalen was charged with street racing and
reckless driving. He later turned himself in, posted a $4,000 bond, and was released. He then entered
a no contest plea agreement and was sentenced to 12 months of probation, a $1,000 fine 80-plus hours
of community service and a defensive driving course. He was later drafted 9th overall by the
Philadelphia Eagles in the 2003 NFL draft.
On the other hand, Victoria filed a $5 million lawsuit against Jalen and the estate of Chandler,
blaming them for racing even though both had histories of traffic offenses.
Her lawsuit cited medical expenses of more than $170,000 and a total of $27,000 in lost wages.
The claim has yet to be settled.
She also sued the UGA Athletic Association for entrusting a rented SUV to Chandler,
despite knowing her history of traffic violations.
A settlement was later reached for $1.5 million.
Devon's father also sued the UGA Athletic Association for $40 million for the same reasons,
and that case remains active to date.
